title: Scalar pullback tensor square before localization
statement: For finite R and p:X→Y, with c the termwise inverse-mate comparison [def-sf-finite-scalar-ordinary-pullback-comparison], the signed-total scalar tensor comparison intertwines the ordinary fixed-scalar and intrinsic pullback tensor maps: V(delta(P,Q));b_X(AP,AQ);t_X(c_P inverse,c_Q inverse) = c_total inverse;B(b_Y(P,Q));m_G(UP,UQ). This is an equality of actual chain maps, for arbitrary P,Q; no derived category or derived tensor model occurs.

source.place: Tags 00YV, 07A4 and 07A6; Scalar pullback tensor square before localization

proof.text: Use the ordinary mate unit equation and the scalar-section direct-image normalization. On a balanced pure tensor both ordinary composites are the tensor of the two inverse-image unit sections. Tensor and sheafification universal properties prove the ordinary square.

Test the two total chain maps on each bidegree coproduct injection. The summand equations for finiteScalarTotalTensorIso and proEtaleTensorPullbackTotalIso reduce to the ordinary square; the Koszul signs agree.

The separate preservation theorem is proved from kFlat_map_of_flat_terms: inverse image preserves flat sheaves and colimits. Apply that theorem to the K-flat complex and check the image terms are flat using the flat-preserving functor instance.
